Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# GLOAMFALL — Endless Survivors

A fast, top-down survival action game inspired by **Vampire Survivors** and **Megabonk**. Pick a survivor, outlast endless waves, hoard glowing relics, and stack upgrades until the night breaks.

![GLOAMFALL gameplay](screenshots/run-desktop-final2.jpg)

## Play

No build step, no external assets. Serve the folder with any static web server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Then open <http://localhost:3002>. On OMGithub, `./start.sh` starts the bundled dev server.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys | Drag the on-screen joystick |
| Use ability | `Space` | Tap the ability orb |
| Pause | `P` / `Esc` | Pause button |
| Choose upgrade | `1` / `2` / `3` or click | Tap a card |

Attacks are automatic. Movement is the only defensive skill you have — keep kiting.

## Survivors

| Survivor | Starting weapon | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Vesper** | Arcane Bolt | Blink Nova |
| **Bramble** | Thorn Orbit | Bramble Guard |
| **Kite** | Scatter Shot | Overdrive |
| **Sable** | Chain Lightning | Singularity |

## Features

- Endless escalating waves, elites, and bosses every ~72 seconds.
- Level-up ascensions: new weapons, passive stacks, and emergency heals.
- Frequent relic drops across **common / rare / epic / legendary** rarities.
- Stacking damage, attack speed, movement, area, crit, lifesteal, burn, frost, chain, and void effects.
- Screen shake, hit flashes, damage numbers, particles, glowing loot beams, and legendary banners.
- Responsive desktop and mobile HUD with safe-area-aware touch controls.
- Synthesized WebAudio soundtrack and SFX — no audio files required.
- Best run saved locally.

## Project layout

```
index.html        DOM shell, HUD, and overlays
styles.css        neon UI, overlays, responsive/mobile layout
src/data.js       characters, weapons, passives, relics, enemies, balance
src/audio.js      WebAudio synth engine and music
src/game.js       loop, combat, spawning, loot, upgrades, rendering, input
```

content.text:
# GLOAMFALL — Endless Survivors

A fast, top-down survival action game inspired by **Vampire Survivors** and **Megabonk**. Pick a survivor, outlast endless waves, hoard glowing relics, and stack upgrades until the night breaks.

## Play

No build step, no external assets. Serve the folder with any static web server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Then open <http://localhost:3002>. On OMGithub, `./start.sh` starts the bundled dev server.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys | Drag the on-screen joystick |
| Use ability | `Space` | Tap the ability orb |
| Pause | `P` / `Esc` | Pause button |
| Choose upgrade | `1` / `2` / `3` or click | Tap a card |

Attacks are automatic. Movement is the only defensive skill you have — keep kiting.

## Survivors

| Survivor | Starting weapon | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Vesper** | Arcane Bolt | Blink Nova |
| **Bramble** | Thorn Orbit | Bramble Guard |
| **Kite** | Scatter Shot | Overdrive |
| **Sable** | Chain Lightning | Singularity |

## Features

- Endless escalating waves, elites, and bosses every ~72 seconds.
- Level-up ascensions: new weapons, passive stacks, and emergency heals.
- Frequent relic drops across **common / rare / epic / legendary** rarities.
- Stacking damage, attack speed, movement, area, crit, lifesteal, burn, frost, chain, and void effects.
- Screen shake, hit flashes, damage numbers, particles, glowing loot beams, and legendary banners.
- Responsive desktop and mobile HUD with safe-area-aware touch controls.
- Synthesized WebAudio soundtrack and SFX — no audio files required.
- Best run saved locally.

## Project layout

```
index.html        DOM shell, HUD, and overlays
styles.css        neon UI, overlays, responsive/mobile layout
src/data.js       characters, weapons, passives, relics, enemies, balance
src/audio.js      WebAudio synth engine and music
src/game.js       loop, combat, spawning, loot, upgrades, rendering, input
```

- **Level-up ascensions** with 3-card choices for new weapons, passive stacks, and emergency healing.
- **Frequent relic loot** across common / rare / epic / legendary rarities.
- **Stacking upgrades** for damage, attack speed, movement, area, crit, lifesteal, burn, frost, chain, and void effects.
- **Juice**: screen shake, hit flashes, damage numbers, particles, glowing loot beams, boss banners, and synthesized WebAudio music/SFX.
- **Desktop + mobile controls**: WASD/arrows, Space ability, pause, and a touch joystick with ability orb.
- Local best-run tracking via `localStorage`.

## Run it

The dev server is already running at **http://localhost:3002**.

Or from the project folder:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

## Controls

- **Move:** WASD / arrow keys / touch joystick
- **Ability:** Space / touch ability orb
- **Pause:** P / Esc / pause button
- **Upgrade choice:** 1–3 or click/tap a card

Attacks are automatic — movement is the main defensive skill.

## Verified

- Desktop title and gameplay at **1280×720**
- Mobile title, gameplay, level-up, pause, boss, and game-over screens at **390×844**
- Upgrade selection, retry, quit, character switching, touch joystick, and ability cooldown
- Zero browser console errors
- `node --check` passes for all JS modules
- Final JPEG checks saved in `screenshots/`

## Assumptions

- Single-player, browser-based game with no build step or external assets.
- Audio is fully synthesized; no audio files are required.
- Balance targets a fast arcade run: early levels arrive within the first ~15–20 seconds, with difficulty ramping through elites and bosses.
- Best-run persistence uses browser `localStorage`.

metadata.displayText:
Improve and balance the existing game. Do not rebuild it from scratch. Keep the current gameplay mechanics, characters, progression system, and overall Vampire Survivors / Megabonk-inspired gameplay, but make the following changes:

1. Reduce Game Speed


- The entire game currently feels too fast.
- Reduce the main character's movement speed.
- Reduce enemy movement speed.
- Make combat feel more deliberate and readable.
- Adjust enemy spawn rates if necessary to maintain a balanced difficulty curve.
- The game should feel exciting but not chaotic or overwhelmingly fast.


2. Improve Visual Clarity and Enemy Identification


- Enemies currently look too similar to environmental objects, projectiles, and experience particles.
- Create a clear visual distinction between different gameplay elements.
- Use distinct color palettes:
  - Enemies: recognizable natural or dark colors.
  - Experience orbs: bright green or another clearly identifiable color.
  - Player projectiles: a separate, consistent color.
  - Enemy projectiles: a different contrasting color.
  - Loot and pickups: unique colors depending on their function.
- Make enemy silhouettes and animations recognizable at a glance.
- Avoid excessive visual effects that make the screen difficult to read.


3. Change the Overall Art Direction


- The current game looks too futuristic, with excessive neon colors and sci-fi aesthetics.
- Move towards a more grounded, organic, and human-oriented visual style.
- Use natural environments, earthy colors, realistic-looking materials, and more traditional fantasy or adventure-inspired visual elements.
- Reduce neon lighting, glowing outlines, futuristic interfaces, and sci-fi effects.
- Characters, enemies, weapons, and environments should feel like they belong in a believable game world.
- Keep the graphics visually appealing, detailed, and atmospheric without making everything look futuristic.


4. Fix Experience and Progression Balance


- After a few levels, enemies start dropping far too much experience.
- The player levels up almost constantly and spends most of the remaining game selecting upgrades instead of actually playing.
- Significantly rebalance experience drops and the experience requirements for each level.
- Make experience progression gradually increase in difficulty as the player levels up.
- Reduce excessive experience drops from regular enemies.
- Make stronger and more dangerous enemies drop more experience than weaker ones.
- Level-ups should feel rewarding and meaningful, not happen every few seconds.
- Maintain a balanced progression curve throughout the entire run, including later stages.


5. Important


- Preserve the existing characters, upgrades, weapons, loot systems, and core gameplay.
- Do not remove existing mechanics unless absolutely necessary.
- Make all changes consistent with each other.
- Test the balance throughout a complete game run, not just the first few minutes.
- The final result should be slower, more readable, more grounded visually, and much better balanced.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and rebalance the existing **GLOAMFALL — Endless Survivors** game without rebuilding it, keeping its characters, weapons, upgrades, loot, and core survivors-like gameplay.
- The updated game should feel slower, more readable, more grounded/organic in art direction, and have a much less spammy level-up curve.

## Requirements
- Reduce player movement speed, enemy movement speed, and overall combat pace; adjust spawn rates if needed.
- Make gameplay elements visually distinct: natural/dark enemies, bright-green XP, consistent player-projectile color, contrasting enemy-projectile color, unique pickup colors.
- Improve enemy silhouettes and animations; reduce excessive effects that obscure readability.
- Shift art direction away from neon/sci-fi toward grounded, earthy, organic fantasy/adventure visuals.
- Reduce regular-enemy XP and significantly raise XP requirements; stronger enemies must give more XP; level-ups must stay meaningful throughout the whole run.
- Preserve existing characters, upgrades, weapons, loot systems, and mechanics.
- Test balance across a complete run, not only the opening minutes.
- Final result must be slower, more readable, more grounded, and better balanced.

## Decisions
- Keep the existing vanilla JS canvas architecture and all gameplay systems.
- Use a consistent readability palette:
  - Player attacks: warm gold `#e6d3a3`
  - Enemy attacks: rust red `#b84f3a`
  - XP: leaf green `#7ed957`, large XP `#b6e35a`
  - Heals: pale sage `#cfe8b8`
- Ground the art direction with forest-floor backgrounds, earthy HUD colors, serif display type, muted rarity colors, and reduced glow/additive effects.
- Slow player speeds to Vesper 172, Bramble 150, Kite 196, Sable 160.
- Slow enemies to grunt 52, runner 92, tank 33, shooter 44, splitter 48, boss 32.
- Slow player projectiles: bolt 540, scatter 480, boomerang 450; enemy shots 140/132.
- Use XP curve `floor(10 + level * 6.5 + level^1.55)`.
- Reduce XP values: grunt `0.7`, runner `0.6`, tank `4`, shooter `2.5`, splitter `3`, boss `90`.
- Use new spawn pacing: interval `max(0.32, 1.12 - time * 0.0024) * rand(0.88, 1.14)`, cap `125 + wave * 6`, count `1 + floor(time / 70)` plus 26% chance for one extra, forced to 1 before 15s.
- Reduce shake to 62%, cap screen flash at `0.18`, reduce burst particle counts to 60%, cap particles at 520.
- Use earthy rarity colors: common `#b9b09a`, rare `#6f9f8a`, epic `#9b6bb3`, legendary `#d8a84e`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Original game is fully built and playable with 4 survivors, auto-attacks, abilities, endless waves, elites/bosses, level-up cards, relics, rarity tiers, mobile touch controls, synthesized audio, and local best-run saving.
- Prior fixes remain: global XP/loot drift, HUD refresh before level-up overlay, favicon, mobile safe-area sizing, and final JPEG screenshot checks.
- Updated `src/data.js` with new earthy character colors, reduced movement speeds, earthy weapon colors, slower projectile speeds, muted rarity colors, natural enemy palettes, reduced enemy speeds, and rebalanced XP values.
- Added readability constants in `src/game.js`: `PLAYER_SHOT_COLOR`, `ENEMY_SHOT_COLOR`, `XP_COLOR`, `XP_BIG_COLOR`, `HEAL_COLOR`.
- Replaced XP curve and spawn pacing in `src/game.js`.
- Slowed enemy projectiles and set all enemy shots to rust red.
- Set bolt/scatter/chakram/chain player effects to the consistent gold palette.
- Reduced shake, screen flash, particle burst counts, and particle cap.
- Rewrote `drawBackground` into a natural forest-floor scene with soil patches, grass, pebbles, roots, mushrooms, and fireflies.
- Recolored `drawGroundAuras` to muted ember/moss.
- Rewrote `drawLoot` into a grounded amulet/relic style with muted beams and no additive compositing.

### Active
- Finish the visual overhaul in `src/game.js`: `drawGems`, `drawHeals`, `drawEnemy`, `drawPlayer`, `drawOrbitWeapons`, `drawProjectiles`, `drawEnemyShots`, `drawEffects`, `drawRings`, `drawParticles`, and `renderTitle`.
- Overhaul `styles.css` from neon sci-fi to parchment/leather/moss fantasy UI.
- Verify syntax after the latest `drawLoot` rewrite.
- Test the new speed, readability, and XP balance through a full run.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check src/game.js src/data.js src/audio.js` and fix any syntax issues.
2. Rewrite `drawGems` as bright-green round motes with dark green rims; rewrite `drawHeals` as pale sage cross pickups.
3. Rework `drawEnemy` to use natural palettes, stronger outlines, subtle bobbing, recognizable silhouettes, and a moth-like shooter; reduce all enemy glow.
4. Replace `drawPlayer` with a grounded humanoid adventurer/cloak/weapon render, keeping current hitbox and ability effects.
5. Reduce/remove additive glow in orbit weapons, projectiles, enemy shots, lightning, rings, and particles; make projectiles visually distinct gold vs rust.
6. Rewrite `renderTitle` as an organic forest/moon/mist scene instead of the sci-fi grid and neon rings.
7. Overhaul `styles.css`: earthy parchment/leather panels, serif display font, muted gold/moss/rust accents, remove scanlines and aggressive neon shadows/clip paths.
8. Reload the game in Playwright at 1280×720 and 390×844; verify color separation, enemy readability, mobile controls, level-up overlay, no console errors.
9. Run a long auto-upgrade run to validate XP pacing, spawn pressure, elites/bosses, and game-over balance; tune values as needed.
10. Update `README.md` if balance/controls text needs adjustment; save final small JPEG screenshots and clean old ones.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: main engine and all remaining visual/rendering work; latest edits are mid-overhaul.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js`: character/enemy/weapon/relic stats and colors; updated balance values live here.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: still mostly neon sci-fi UI; needs the main art-direction overhaul.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM/HUD/overlay structure; favicon added.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: game documentation; may need minor updates after balance changes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: current final JPEG checks from the previous pass; regenerate after the visual overhaul.
- `/tmp/opencode/gloam-backup/`: backup of pre-overhaul `src/`, `styles.css`, `index.html`, `README.md` for comparison/rollback.

## Important Context
- Dev server is running at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright session is `gloam`.
- Headless Chromium runs slowly; the game loop caps `dt` at `0.05`, so game time advances at roughly 0.35× real time during tests. Long runs require patience.
- All work is uncommitted; most game files are untracked and `README.md` is modified.
- `.gitignore` ignores `screenshots/`.
- Current new balance values are already applied in `src/data.js` and parts of `src/game.js`; remaining old neon rendering is still visible until the rest of the rewrite is completed.
- `drawGems` still uses the old diamond/gold-big-gem style; `drawHeals`, `drawEnemy`, `drawPlayer`, and `renderTitle` still retain much of the previous neon/sci-fi look.
- `drawParticles` and `drawRings` still use additive `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`; `drawProjectiles`, `drawEnemyShots`, and `drawEffects` still need glow reduction.
- XP/loot drift and `updateHud()` inside `openLevelUp()` remain important existing fixes; do not regress them.
- Previous final screenshots included desktop title/gameplay, mobile title/gameplay, level-up, pause, boss, and game-over.

metadata.displayText:
The game has improved, but several important issues still need to be fixed. Please make the following adjustments:

1. Reduce Game Speed


- The game is still too fast, even after the previous adjustments.
- Reduce the movement speed of both the player and enemies further.
- Make the overall gameplay more relaxed and tactical, giving players enough time to react.
- Avoid overwhelming the player with enemies too quickly.


2. Slow Down Level Progression


- Player levels currently increase way too quickly.
- Significantly increase the XP required for each level.
- Make progression slower and more rewarding.
- Higher levels should require noticeably more experience than earlier levels.
- Balance XP rewards so that players cannot level up every few seconds.


3. Reduce Power-Up Drops


- Enemies still drop far too many power-ups.
- Significantly reduce the drop rate of all power-ups and special items.
- Make powerful and rare items genuinely rare.
- Each drop should feel meaningful rather than constantly filling the screen.


4. Fix Power-Up Notifications


- When enemies drop power-ups, the notifications describing those items appear at the top of the screen and cover almost half of the gameplay area.
- Completely redesign these notifications.
- Make them much smaller, shorter and less intrusive.
- Display only a small icon and a brief item name.
- Notifications should disappear quickly and never obstruct the player's view.
- Do not stack multiple large notifications on top of each other.


5. Redesign the Interface


- The game world looks less futuristic now, which is good.
- However, the user interface still has an overly futuristic purple and blue appearance.
- Remove the dominant purple, violet, neon blue and cyberpunk visual elements.
- Replace them with a more grounded, natural and classic game interface.
- Use earthy, neutral and muted colors, such as dark brown, olive green, beige, muted red and warm grey.
- Make the interface feel like a polished fantasy adventure or survival game rather than a futuristic sci-fi game.
- Keep the UI clean, readable and visually consistent with the game world.


6. Add Russian Language Support


- Add a language selection option in the main menu or settings.
- Support at least two languages: English and Russian.
- Translate all menus, buttons, settings, character descriptions, item names, power-ups, notifications, level-up choices and gameplay messages.
- Make sure Russian text displays correctly, including Cyrillic characters.
- Allow players to switch languages at any time without restarting the game.
- Ensure that all newly added content also supports both languages.


Important: Do not completely redesign the game or remove existing mechanics, characters, upgrades or content. Preserve the current gameplay systems and improve only the areas described above. Make the changes noticeable, not barely perceptible. Prioritize gameplay balance, readability and a comfortable playing experience.
